Subject: Post-demo follow-up — data handling and training preferences

Thanks again for taking the demo today, Samira — really appreciated the thoughtful questions from the BrightPay team. Quick recap and next steps from our side: 

- Internal ask: confirm whether BrightPay wants Redwood to use event/usage data for model improvements (model tuning/fine-tuning). Please reply with a simple "opt-in" or "opt-out".
- Data residency: we can pin BrightPay traffic to our us-west region; confirm if you need EU residency instead.
- Logging & retention: default request logs retained 30 days; we can extend or shorten per contract.

I've attached a short matrix that maps each control we discussed to the contract clause (see attachment: privacy-controls-matrix.csv). Avery is copied to provide technical detail on the logging retention and masking controls.

Next steps: if you can confirm training preference and residency by end of week we will prepare the DPA redline and an updated SOW with the retention terms.

Best,
Jordan

From: Samira Khan <samira.k@brightpay.com>

Cc: BrightPay Legal <legal@brightpay.com>, Avery Johnson <avery.johnson@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-07-12T17:08:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo follow-up — data handling and training preferences

Hi Jordan — thanks for the summary. A few clarifications from our side before we confirm: 

1) BrightPay's policy is that any customer PII must not be used to train external models. Can you confirm how Redwood separates PII from telemetry and whether any de-identified data could still be used for model training?
2) For request logging: we need a 90-day retention window for auditability, with the ability to purge on request. Can Redwood support a 90-day default for our tenancy?
3) Data residency: start with US but we may need EU residency later — what's the process for migration/dual residency?

Looping in Legal to review DPA. For now please treat this as a potential opt-out for training on raw customer data; we may consider a limited, reviewed opt-in for aggregated/derivative signals only.

Thanks,
Samira
Head of Product — BrightPay
[samira.k@brightpay.com]

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>
To: Samira Khan <samira.k@brightpay.com>
Cc: Avery Johnson <avery.johnson@redwoodinference.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-07-13T09:14:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo follow-up — data handling and training preferences

Hi Samira — great questions, and thanks for the tentative direction. Short answers up front then details below: 

- Training-on-customer-data: we can absolutely honor an opt-out. If BrightPay opts out, Redwood will not use any BrightPay raw or de-identified customer content to further train or fine-tune our shared/public models. We can include a clause in the DPA/SOW that explicitly prohibits model tuning on your data.
- De-identification: we perform automated PII masking for supported fields (emails, SSNs, credit card numbers) in the runtime logs. HOWEVER, de-identified data is still considered customer-derived material and will not be used for model training unless explicitly permitted in writing.
- Retention & purge: we can set BrightPay tenancy logging retention to 90 days and expose a self-service purge API for tenant-level redaction requests. We will document the SLA for purge completion (typically 72 hours).
- Data residency: we can pin to us-west now; for EU residency we offer a migration path that provisions a EU-dedicated tenancy and performs controlled data transfer under our DPA/Standard Contractual Clauses. Migration lead time is ~3–5 weeks depending on dataset size.

Attachments included: DPA_redwood_v3.pdf (redlineable), SOC2-snapshot-2026-06.pdf (controls reference), and privacy-controls-matrix.csv that maps controls to UI/infra settings.

If BrightPay confirms "opt-out for model training" and "90-day retention in US", we'll: 
1) Produce a DPA draft with an explicit no-training clause and the 90-day retention clause.
2) Add a paragraph in the SOW about the purge API and the 72-hour purge SLA.
3) Share a migration checklist for EU residency (if/when you need it).

Avery — can you confirm the purge API endpoint and sample request so I can include it in the DPA appendix?

Thanks,
Jordan
[Attachment: DPA_redwood_v3.pdf (application/pdf); Attachment: SOC2-snapshot-2026-06.pdf (application/pdf)]

From: BrightPay Legal <legal@brightpay.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Samira Khan <samira.k@brightpay.com>
Date: 2026-07-14T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Post-demo follow-up — data handling and training preferences

Jordan / Redwood team — thanks for the rapid follow-up. On behalf of BrightPay Legal we confirm the following positions after internal review: 

- BrightPay will opt-out of any use of customer-provided content (raw or de-identified) for model training, tuning, or improvement. Please include an explicit prohibition in Section 4.2 of the DPA.
- BrightPay requires a 90-day retention default for logs tied to our tenancy, with a documented purge API and 72-hour completion SLA.
- For the EU residency option, please include migration timelines and applicable transfer safeguards (SCCs) in the DPA appendix.

Please send a DPA draft with those changes and we will review redlines. Also include a checklist for technical validation (purge API sample requests, masking rules, and where audit logs appear in the Console). We anticipate completing legal review within 5 business days of receiving the redlined DPA.

Regards,
BrightPay Legal
